role: Identity specialist B — small-size recognition and typography hierarchy
observedStrengths: The head-only avatar is a sound reduction of the existing anatomy. The unequal paddles, tilted eyes and scalloped cream face form an apparently distinctive arrangement without exaggerating or replacing the tiny moth.

Both complete antennae fit the circular crops in the supplied 32–160 px ladder. At 48–64 px the face and asymmetry remain readable; the day version is especially coherent. The night keyline visibly improves stem continuity over the previous treatment.

At the supplied 390 px README width, heyNag reads immediately in both themes. The simple wordmark, generous scale and compact moth establish a clear primary identity; question headings then organize the software work without competing visually.

The application source clones the existing head and outlines the existing wordmark. This is a coherent application system rather than a separately redrawn avatar. The paired headers visibly retain the same layout and character proportions.

concreteConcerns.claim: The 32 px night avatar has little margin for further reduction: the cream face remains strong, but the thin antenna connections are much less immediate than the paddles. This is a small-size robustness concern, not evidence that the supplied 32 px export fails.
concreteConcerns.evidence: refinement/evidence/identity.png, original-resolution 32 px night circular crop versus day; assets/brand/heynag-moth-avatar-v5-night.png shows the thin pale edge around a dark stem. applications-v5.json records 32 px as the minimum tested size.

concreteConcerns.claim: The head crop preserves individual character cues but removes the wings that identify the creature as a moth. Without prior exposure, it could read as a sprout-like friendly creature. The association between avatar, moth and heyNag is plausible but unmeasured.
concreteConcerns.evidence: Head-only day/night exports versus the full-body header. No participant recognition, category-label or delayed-recall results were supplied.

concreteConcerns.claim: The wordmark supplies excellent reading clarity but little obvious proprietary character on its own. Much of the apparent individuality currently depends on the moth and lime/cream palette. This supports keeping the lockup consistent; it does not justify decorative lettering merely to appear unique.
concreteConcerns.evidence: header-v5-light.png and both readme-390 captures: straightforward grotesk heyNag, with personality concentrated in the adjacent illustration. No comparison or recognition study isolates the wordmark.

qualityCriteriaForNine: Retain the tiny anatomy, complete asymmetric antennae, and identical theme geometry; do not enlarge body parts to rescue small applications.
Document a defensible minimum avatar size from native-size, circular-mask evidence on realistic light and dark surroundings; show 16/24 px as boundary tests, not automatic required use cases.
Keep the existing readable mobile wordmark hierarchy and establish when the full lockup, head avatar and wordmark alone are appropriate.
Treat apparent distinctiveness separately from measured recognition. Any claims of reliable owner association or memorability require human evidence.
highestValueExperiment: Run one compact reduction-and-association study: existing exports at 24/32/48/64 px on actual application surrounds, followed by a small formative human test linking the unlabelled avatar to the full heyNag lockup after brief exposure and a delay. Record antenna continuity separately from name association. Adjust only the failing usage or paint treatment, if any; preserve geometry.
limits: Independent observation saved before reading other reviewers. Static local evidence only; no browser, live GitHub, motion or human testing. Scores cannot establish audience attachment. No objection to the present identity direction or readable header hierarchy.
